function: Learned NOMA-vs-OMA mode decision (DNN) and NOMA power-allocation factor (DDQN with varying bounds) for a satellite downlink, maximizing sum effective capacity under delay QoS (pp. 5-7).
system: p. 3: single-antenna satellite and users in one spot beam, downlink NOMA/OMA, Shadowed-Rician link, SNR 20-50 dB; no RIS; carrier frequency not stated.
method: p. 6-7: one-hidden-layer DNN classifier (supervised, 25 000 samples) and DDQN with varying action bounds (reinforcement); K-GMM clustering for user pairing.
data_channel: p. 3, 6, 8: custom simulation with Shadowed-Rician fading (light, average, heavy shadowing, parameters from a prior work); DNN trained on 25 000 randomly generated samples; no 3GPP model.
test_conditions: p. 6-10: DNN trained on 22 000 and validated on 3000 simulated samples (35-50 dB); DDQN learns online over episodes in each setting; no new-condition test described.
baselines: p. 9-10: non-learned exhaustive search power allocation, pure OMA and pure NOMA; learned DDPG, single DQN, and DDQN with fixed bounds, the latter three compared on convergence speed.
metrics: p. 6-11: sum effective capacity (bps/Hz), per-user effective capacity, convergence over episodes, DNN validation accuracy (Table I).
complexity: p. 7-8: number of multiplications as big-O orders: K-GMM O((IT+IG)KM), DNN training and prediction, DDQN O(Ne*Nt*...); total Oc + Od + Or; no runtime or parameter count.
q1_support: p. 3: "By modeling the link coefficient gt,j as the widely applied Shadowed-Rician fading distribution". Custom link model; fading parameters "can refer to [20]" (p. 8), a prior conference paper; no 3GPP TR 38.811 or 38.901, DeepMIMO, or measured data is mentioned.
q2_support: p. 6: "The number of data in each set are further set as 22 000 and 3000, respectively." Training and validation come from the same generator; DDQN results (Figs. 8-11, pp. 9-11) are per setting, and no model is tested on a scenario, user count or band not used for training.
q3_support: p. 9: "Fig. 8 compares the convergence rates of Deep Deterministic Policy Gradient (DDPG) [41], single DQN (SDQN) [42]" so the learned comparisons are on convergence only. Exhaustive search, OMA and NOMA are compared on capacity (Figs. 9, 11), but the only learned comparison on capacity (Fig. 9) is DDQN with fixed bounds, an ablation of the proposed DDQN.
q4_support: p. 7: "The complexity of the proposed solution for problem P1 is measured in terms of the number of multiplications involved in K-GMM, DNN, and DDQN-varying bounds"; p. 8: "the total complexity of the proposed algorithm is Oc + Od + Or".
q5_support: p. 6: "whose input data are randomly generated within the range of" (the DNN data); no code or data link, public dataset, or measured data is given.
notes: Title and DOI match on p. 1. Included under area 6: the DDQN power allocation and the DNN NOMA/OMA decision control a satellite downlink, a physical-layer decision (power) learned jointly with an access decision; K-GMM is classical clustering. Single-antenna nodes (p. 3) are admitted for NTN works; RIS appears only in cited titles. q3 is 0 because DDPG, SDQN and DDQN with fixed bounds are compared on convergence speed (Fig. 8) and DDQN with fixed bounds [43] in Fig. 9 is the proposed DDQN without its varying-bounds module; the reviewer may flip q3 if [43] is taken as an earlier learned method. DNN data cover 35-50 dB while Figs. 10-11 use 30 dB, which is an SNR change and not a q2 case.
